title.narrative: Strengthening lifesaving nutrition services in Pulka, Gwoza LGA, Borno State, Northeast Nigeria

description.narrative:
ltpgtltpgtltspangtltspangtThe overall objective of this project is to contribute lt/spangtltspangtltspangtto improving the nutrition status of the conflict-affected population, IDPs and Host Community, in Borno State, Northeast Nigeria, by improving their access to curative and preventive nutritional services. This objective aligns with the 2023 United Nations Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and NHF first Reserve Allocation strategy to address the rapidly deteriorating nutrition situation.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtCurative nutritional services will be provided to children under 5 suffering from Severe or Moderate Acute Malnutrition (SAM or MAM). lt/spangtltspangtSAM cases with medical complications will be provided ltspangt24/7 treatment in Pulka Stabilization Centre (SC), located in Pulka PHCC, that PUI has been supporting since December 2022. The SC bed capacity will be increased from 20 to 40 beds to meet with the increasing number of admissions. Referrals of cases to secondary health care will be ensured whenever needed, and transportation allowance provided. Caretakers of SAM children with medical complications will be supported with the provision of food and hygiene supplies, to avoid any negative coping mechanism. Children suffering from SAM without medical complications will be provided treatment in 2 Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs), one PUI supported between December 2022 and May 2023 in Damara MCH, and one PUI will start supporting under this project in Pulka PHCC to meet the increased number of OTP admissions. Admitted children will receive treatment based on the National CMAM guidelines. To ensure the quality of the assistance provided, PUI will ensure the training of MoH staff on Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM), and of Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNM) on community mobilization/outreach component. This will also contribute to rooting the project into the community and ensuring the continuity of service when or if PUI exits.lt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtltspangtTreatment of children under 5 suffering from MAM will be provided through the Tom Brown approach, which PUI has been successfully implementing since January 2021 in Monguno. ltbgtPUI coordinated with another partner (ASHF) implementing TSFP program in Gwoza LGA under NHF grant to ensure there is no duplication of TSFP services in Pulka. lt/bgtFollowing this approach, mothers / caregivers of children suffering from MAM are gathered into groups where they are taught by Lead Mothers how to prepare a nutrient rich supplemental food with local ingredients over a 12 to 13 weeks program. Along with this cooking recipe, ltspangtmothers / caretakers are sensitized on lt/spangtltspangtthe use of clean water and hygiene practices. They are then encouraged to cascade the knowledge they have acquired to other community members. lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtltspangtPreventive ltspangtnutritional services will consist in the active screening of children aged 06-59 months to ensure the early detection of SAM cases by 25 trained Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMs) living within the community. The CNMs will also ensure awareness raising sessions within the community on Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) best practices, including exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life, and conduct cooking demonstrations in the community. They will oversee 50 Mother Care Groups (MCGs) of 15 mothers each, with lead mothers in charge of promoting child and mother health care services and the dissemination of key nutrition messages.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtltspangtThe strong involvement of the community through the network of CNMs and MCGs will ensure the beneficiaries’ ownership of the proposed project, as well as maximize its short- and long-term impacts, also in terms of social norm change. lt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtltspangtThe project will integrate Protection and Gender targeted activities to mainstream, among others GBV prevention and lt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtltspangtmitigation measures in the nutrition responseltspangt. Therefore, safe and dignified quality nutrition services will be accessible for all, including lt/spangtltspangtpeople at heightenedlt/spangtltspangt risk of violence and child nutrition status will be improved through positive social norms.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtlt/pgt
